taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-16, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 312.0 | 6.08 | 6.08
2 | 794.3 | 14.76 | 20.84
3 | 884.4 | 3.48 | 24.32
4 | 1280.2 | 10.95 | 35.27
5 | 4929.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-16, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-16, Survey Area T**

The interpreted VES model at T-16 comprises five layers with resistivities increasing monotonically with depth: 312.0 Ω·m (0–6.08 m), 794.3 Ω·m (6.08–20.84 m), 884.4 Ω·m (20.84–24.32 m), 1280.2 Ω·m (24.32–35.27 m), and 4929.0 Ω·m (basement, below 35.27 m). This sequence indicates a steadily resistive profile with no intermediate low-resistivity layer, consistent with a shallow conductive/moderately resistive overburden grading into a highly resistive substratum, likely competent bedrock.

Applying the curve-type convention to the three consecutive layer triplets (1-2-3, 2-3-4, 3-4-5), each triplet shows r1 < r2 < r3, yielding "A" for all three comparisons (AAA), which simplifies to a single-letter "A" type curve. This matches the on-file classification of AAA-type. No discrepancy is noted between the computed curve type and the filed label.

{"curve_type_stated": "AAA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
